Yes, switch to Claude Desktop. But running inside Orca isn't really the problem. The bigger issue is that this session runs in the old WSL copy of the repo.

**Why running inside Orca is fine**
- Orca normally keeps its terminals in a separate background process. Quitting, restarting or updating Orca leaves that process running, so a Claude session survives and reconnects. I checked this in Orca's source. The one thing that does end your terminals is Settings → Terminal → Manage Sessions → Restart daemon.
- Our plugin runs in its own process with timeouts, so a broken plugin can't take your terminals down.

**What's actually wrong with this session**
- It runs in `~/orca-entire-extension`, the old WSL copy. Entire records this chat against that repo, not the Windows one where the code now lives.
- Every test and every `entire` or `orca` command has to cross from WSL into Windows, and Orca's WSL settings leak into those Windows programs. For example, the Windows `entire status` I ran from here picked up this session's Linux Claude config path and rejected it.

**For the new session**
- In Claude Desktop, start a **Local** session (not WSL) on `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`. You have Desktop 4.29 installed, plus Claude Code 2.1.311 on Windows if you'd rather use a terminal.
- Desktop reads the same settings files as the CLI, so the repo's Entire hooks should work. To confirm, run `entire status` after your first prompt and check that it lists the session. If Desktop was already open when you installed the Entire nightly, restart it so it picks up the new PATH.
- With Claude outside Orca, you can also restart Orca's terminal daemon, upgrade Orca, or run a test build of Orca without affecting Claude.
- Staying in Orca would also work, if you open a workspace on the Windows repo (it's already registered in Orca). Either way, stop using this WSL session.

**What I added so the new session has the context**
A Windows session won't see my memory or this chat, so I put what it needs into the repo:
- **`CLAUDE.md`** points to `docs/PLAN.md` and lists the commands, gotchas and rules. The rules: Entire setup commands are yours to run, Claude asks before writing anything to Entire, and trail text is treated as untrusted.
- **The test harness** was in my temporary folder and would have disappeared with this session. It's now in `scripts/orca-harness/`. It runs the plugin inside `Orca.exe` the way Orca does, without the UI: `node scripts/orca-harness/launch.mjs no-terminal`.
- **Docs:** I updated the README, and `docs/PLAN.md` now says Windows runs the Entire nightly.
- **Checked:** all 9 tests pass and the harness worked in every scenario. Pointed at this session's own Orca terminal, it reached the WSL Entire nightly (205 ms) and found the repo enabled. It found no trail on `main`, as expected.

**Your setup is good.** The Entire nightly and `git-remote-entire` are on the Windows PATH, and no older copy gets in the way. Claude Code's hooks are up to date. Codex's hooks in this repo are out of date, which only matters if you use Codex here. The fix is `entire agent add codex`. It rewrites the committed `.codex/hooks.json`, so run it on a branch.

**Before you close this session**
- Nothing is committed. Have the new session commit on a branch, so the Entire checkpoint ends up in the Windows repo with the code.
- This planning chat would only become an Entire checkpoint through a commit in the WSL copy. If you don't need it on record there, you can delete that copy. The raw chat log stays in `~/.claude` either way.

Suggested first prompt for the new session: *"Read CLAUDE.md and docs/PLAN.md. We're at the phase 0.5 smoke test."*
</pasted_content id="a49e">

1	# Entire for Orca: plan
2	
3	Bring Entire (trails, findings, approvals, checkpoints) into Orca's UI as an Orca plugin, the way
4	Orca already surfaces GitHub pull requests and checks.
5	
6	Status: phase 0 done. Next: the smoke test, then phase 1 spikes.
7	
8	## Environment
9	
10	- Orca desktop runs on Windows (1.4.245). Plugins are in alpha: manifest format 2, host API 1.0.
11	- Most Orca and Entire projects live in WSL (`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\...`). Orca also has an SSH host.
12	- Entire CLI `0.12.3-nightly` on both sides: WSL (keyring login) and Windows in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`
13	  (Credential Manager login).
14	- This repo: `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`, origin
15	  `entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/et/entire-repos/orca-entire-extension`, Entire enabled.
16	
17	## What Orca's plugin API allows today (1.4.245)
18	
19	Sources: `docs/reference/plugin-*.md` and `src/shared/plugins/**` in github.com/stablyai/orca.
20	
21	- `execution: "trusted-worker"`: `main` runs in a Node process Orca forks on the desktop host (Windows
22	  here). It has full Node access, but its env is an allowlist (PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, TEMP and a few
23	  Windows system variables; no APPDATA). Idle workers stop after 5 minutes with nothing in flight, and a
24	  command must answer within 30 seconds.
25	- Host API 1.0: `workspace.readContext` returns `{ branch, displayName, terminals: [{ id }] }` with no
26	  path; `notifications.show`; `terminal.sendText` (worker only); `storage.*`, `secrets.*` and
27	  `settings.*` (worker only).
28	- Events (at most 3): `workspace.created`, `workspace.removed`, `agent.status.changed`.
29	- Panels are sealed: Orca injects CSP `connect-src 'none'`, blocks links and `window.open`, and gives a
30	  panel no channel to its own worker. A panel cannot show Entire data yet.
31	- Reserved but not shipped: `taskSources`, `statusBarItems`, `sidebarCards`, `connections`, `settings`,
32	  `hooks`, `skills`, `mcpServers`.
33	- The installed build has no `orca plugin ...` CLI (it is on Orca's `main`). Load the plugin through
34	  Settings → Plugins → Development folders.
35	- On 1.4.245 the manifest must keep `publisher` (leaving it out needs `>=1.4.246`). When distributing,
36	  it must equal the GitHub owner of the repository Orca installs from. Ids may not start with `orca-`.
37	
38	## Spike results (2026-10-30)
39	
40	Run from Windows Node with the worker's env allowlist:
41	
42	- `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire trail list ... --json` works with the WSL
43	  login, in 0.6–0.8 s per call.
44	- Orca's CLI (`resources\bin\orca.exe` beside the app) works once APPDATA is derived from USERPROFILE.
45	  `worktree list` takes about 2.1 s.
46	- `readContext` terminal ids are Orca CLI terminal handles. `orca terminal show --terminal <id> --json`
47	  returns the workspace's `worktreePath` (e.g. `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\peterc\ccw`), which gives the
48	  distro and Linux path.
49	- Entire has `--json` on `status`, `trail list/show/approvals/finding`, and `trail watch --json`
50	  (the trail's SSE stream as JSON lines). `trail show` exits 1 when the branch has no trail.
51	
52	## Architecture
53	
54	- One `trusted-worker` plugin. The worker is the only part that talks to Entire.
55	- Find the focused workspace's path: first terminal handle from `readContext` → `orca terminal show`.
56	  Fallback: match branch and name against `orca worktree list`. This is a stopgap until `readContext`
57	  carries a path (see the asks below).
58	- Run Entire where the repo and its login live. For a WSL path, use
59	  `wsl.exe -d <distro> --cd <path> -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire ...`. For a local path, run
60	  `entire` directly. SSH workspaces come later.
61	- Shell out to the Entire CLI rather than calling its REST API. The CLI owns login, contexts and cell
62	  routing, so the plugin never holds a token. `entire api` covers gaps.
63	- Cache per repo and branch, refresh on `agent.status.changed`, and tail `trail watch --json` while the
64	  worker is alive.
65	- Panels only render what worker commands return. Feature-detect with `orca.host.has(...)` so one build
66	  runs on shipped and newer Orca.
67	- Entire text (intent, findings, comments) is untrusted: render it as text and never execute it.
68	
69	## GitHub feature → Entire equivalent
70	
71	| Orca + GitHub today             | Entire equivalent                                  | Unblocked by                     |
72	| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
73	| PR and CI notifications         | trail events → notifications                       | shipped API                      |
74	| Create, approve, merge a PR     | `trail create`, `approve`, `merge` as commands     | shipped API                      |
75	| Checks sidebar, review comments | trail panel: gates, CI runs, findings, approvals   | Orca #25256                      |
76	| Issues on Tasks → new workspace | trails tab → start a workspace on the change       | Orca #26282                      |
77	| PR badge on the workspace card  | trail badge on the card                            | #26282, then a forge provider    |
78	
79	For `et/` repos (`entire://` remotes, like this one) Orca has no forge integration at all, so this
80	plugin is the only one. For GitHub repos it sits beside Orca's GitHub support.
81	
82	## Phases
83	
84	- [x] 0. Repo on Windows, Entire enabled in WSL and on Windows, project added to Orca.
85	- [ ] 0.5 Smoke test: load the dev plugin and run **Entire: Check connection** in a WSL workspace and in
86	      this one.
87	- [ ] 1. Spikes: real trail JSON fixtures (create a test trail), `trail watch` through `wsl.exe` versus
88	      the 5-minute reaper, the plugin consent flow, latency budget.
89	- [ ] 2. v0.1 on shipped Orca: commands (show trail, findings, approve, merge, create, refresh) and
90	      notifications when an agent finishes and on trail events.
91	- [ ] 3. Trail panel. Needs a panel → worker channel (Orca #25256).
92	- [ ] 4. Trails tab on the Tasks page and a settings form (Orca #26282).
93	- [ ] 5. Deeper: status bar item, forge provider for `entire://` remotes, Entire agent hooks and skills,
94	      checkpoints, `entire why`, `entire review`.
95	- [ ] 6. Distribution: a GitHub mirror (Orca installs over https Git and derives the publisher from the
96	      owner), then a catalog listing.
97	
98	## Asks for the Orca team
99	
100	1. A channel from a panel to its own worker (#25256, or a push channel). It blocks any live panel.
101	2. `workspace.readContext`: add the worktree id, path and host (local, WSL, SSH).
102	3. Task sources and plugin settings (#26282), with a start recipe that can check out an existing branch.
103	4. Status bar items and sidebar cards (#23143, #26951).
104	5. Opening external URLs from panels and workers (#27568).
105	6. Long-lived worker subscriptions: the 5-minute idle reaper stops `trail watch`.
106	7. A way to run a command on the workspace's host (WSL, SSH) from a worker.
107	
108	## Risks and open questions
109	
110	- Phases 3–5 depend on unmerged Orca PRs: #25256 quiet since Oct 7, #26282 active, #15315 (forge
111	  providers) stale since August.
112	- The WSL bridge does not cover SSH workspaces.
113	- WSL runs Entire 0.12.3-nightly and Windows runs 0.12.2. On Windows, `entire status` reports the Claude
114	  Code and Codex hooks as out of date. Align the versions before running `entire doctor`, since it
115	  rewrites committed hook files.
116	- A worker's PATH comes from Orca's environment at launch. Restart Orca after installing Entire on
117	  Windows.
118	- Can #26282's start recipe check out an existing branch, or only branch off a base?

7	export function run(command, args, { cwd, env = process.env, signal, timeoutMs = CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {

11	    const stdout = []
12	    const stderr = []
13	    let timedOut = false

18	    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => stdout.push(chunk))
19	    child.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => stderr.push(chunk))
20	    child.on('error', (error) => {

28	        timedOut,
29	        stdout: Buffer.concat(stdout).toString('utf8'),

1	# Entire for Orca
2	
3	An Orca plugin that brings Entire trails, findings and checkpoints into Orca. The plan, the API limits
4	it works within, and the spike results are in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md).
5	
6	## Try it
7	
8	Requires Orca 1.4.245 or later, and the Entire CLI logged in wherever your repos live (WSL or Windows).
9	
10	1. In Orca, open **Settings → Plugins** and turn plugins on.
11	2. Click **Development folders…**, add this folder, then review and enable **Entire**.
12	3. Focus a workspace and run **Entire: Check connection** from the command palette.
13	
14	Orca reloads the plugin when its manifest changes; after editing the worker, use **Restart** on the
15	plugin's row.
16	
17	## Develop
18	
19	No build step yet: the worker is plain ES modules under `src/worker`.
20	
21	```sh
22	node --test
23	```
24	
25	To run the worker inside Orca's own runtime without the GUI (Windows, Orca installed):
26	
27	```sh
28	node scripts/orca-harness/launch.mjs no-terminal
29	```

content.text:
The new session works. `entire status` lists this session (`b9941814…`), so Entire's hooks run from Claude Desktop. Everything up to the Orca step of the phase 0.5 smoke test works.

**What I checked**
- **Tests:** all 9 pass with Node 26.
- **Harness:** I ran it inside `Orca.exe` in every scenario.
  - `none` and `no-terminal` give the expected errors. Without a terminal, "main on main" matches 13 workspaces.
  - Pointed at a real Orca terminal in the Windows workspace, it found the repo enabled, read in 421 ms.
  - Pointed at a WSL `cc-palace` terminal, it ran Entire in WSL and found that repo enabled too, in 446 ms.
  - Neither branch has a trail, so the Trail line just reports that, as intended.
- **Plugin in Orca:** Orca has already installed it from `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`, and its copy matches the repo's `src/` and manifest. You don't need to press Restart.

**The smoke test in Orca**
Orca's CLI can't run plugin commands, so this part is yours:
1. Focus the Windows **orca-entire-extension** workspace. It already has a terminal open, which the plugin needs to find the workspace's path.
2. From the command palette, run **Entire: Check connection**. You should see the same lines as the harness: the path, `Entire CLI 0.12.3-nightly…`, and `Repo: enabled · agents: Claude Code, Codex`.
3. Do the same in a WSL workspace such as `cc-palace`. The path should show as `WSL Ubuntu /home/peterc/…`.

If either one reports that it can't start `entire`, Orca was probably already running when you installed the Windows nightly. Restart Orca to fix it; your terminals survive the restart.

**One fix to the plan**
The Risks section of [PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md:113) still said Windows runs 0.12.2. I updated it: both sides run the nightly. Codex's 7 hooks in this repo are actually waiting for you to approve them in Codex's `/hooks`, rather than out of date. That only matters if you use Codex here.

**Committing**
Nothing is committed yet. If I commit, Entire attaches this session to the commit as a checkpoint, which counts as writing to Entire, so I'm asking first.

Add the Entire for Orca plugin scaffold and connection check

A trusted-worker Orca plugin with one command, "Entire: Check connection".
It finds the focused workspace's path through an Orca terminal handle (or
branch and name as a fallback), runs Entire there (through wsl.exe for WSL
workspaces), and reports the CLI version, the repo's Entire status and the
branch's trail.

Also adds unit tests, a harness that runs the worker inside Orca.exe with
a fake host API, CLAUDE.md, the README and docs/PLAN.md.
